$comment: Consciously accepted findings from the Supabase security advisor, and how many of
each are tolerated. Checked by .github/workflows/advisors.yml on a schedule and via
A lint name absent from here, or a count above max_count, fails the job. Accepting
a finding means editing this file with a reason, which is the point -- it should be
a reviewed artefact rather than a suppression list nobody reads.
To regenerate after an intentional change: run the advisor, then update max_count to
the observed number. Do not paste the numbers in without reading what they are.

why: These are the api.* write wrappers, and being SECURITY DEFINER is the design.
`private` carries no USAGE grant to client roles, so an INVOKER wrapper cannot
reach the privileged code it needs; the wrapper IS the security boundary, and it
is only safe because each one authorises the caller's role and scopes itself to
the caller's tenant.
The per-function allow-list is enforced structurally by
supabase/tests/rls_coverage.test.sql ('only the allow-listed wrappers in the api
schema are SECURITY DEFINER'), which runs in CI on every push and is fail-closed.
So this count is a tripwire for a function added outside that allow-list, not a
blanket acceptance.
Note the asymmetry, which is deliberate: no SECURITY DEFINER function in an
exposed schema may be executable by `anon`. There is no legitimate reason for any
of them to answer a request with no session. The platform's own
public.rls_auto_enable() violated exactly that and was fixed in migration
Genuinely not fixed, and not fixable from here: the toggle lives in the Supabase
dashboard and has no SQL or MCP surface.
BLOCKING FOR GO-LIVE IF THE PLAN ALLOWS IT. Project Settings -> Authentication
-> Email provider settings -> 'Prevent use of leaked passwords'. It requires the
Pro plan; on Free the toggle is absent.
Until it is enabled this entry must stay here, and it must be consciously
accepted with the reason recorded -- which is what the Security Advisor item in
docs/go-live-checklist.md asks for.
Not fixed. Same reason: dashboard-only, no SQL or MCP surface.
Project Settings -> Authentication -> MFA -> enable the TOTP factor. TOTP alone
clears this finding and works with any authenticator app; phone and WebAuthn are
not needed.
This is only half of MFA. Enabling the factor is the dashboard's job; *requiring*
it for TENANT_ADMIN is this application's job, via the `aal` restrictive policy
referenced in docs/go-live-checklist.md. That half is still open and is tracked
there.
